label: rare: copy-phase input "1" late in long sequences (weak)
explanation: Very sparse feature (~0.02% of steps). About half its activations are on copy-phase steps where the fed-back input is the digit 1 (17.7x lift), concentrated late in long sequences (recall_idx 5-8, L=8-9). The rest are on <DEL> (~20% of mass), original-phase f, and scattered letters after repeated letters (e.g. g a a g). Even the best predicate is very imprecise: only ~2% of copy-phase 1 inputs activate it, so what it depends on is some hidden-state context that no tested variable captures (prev_tok a/c/l, out_tok u/j and prefix content each help only slightly). Magnitude is fairly flat across conditions (median 0.12, max 0.22). It never fires at t=0-1 or after a copy error.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: phase=2 & in_tok=1 (+5.64), in_tok=f (+3.93), prev_tok=a (+3.50), phase=2 & in_tok=u (+3.10), prev_tok=c (+3.02), out_tok=u (+2.73). Lower it: phase=2 (-3.52), prev3_tok=u (-2.85), recall_idx=1 (-2.82), prev2_tok=j (-2.66).
